metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate measures the share of provisioned compute doing real work over time, not at peak, and it is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.

Idle servers burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. Fleet utilization is where the money hides in most enterprise estates, so this metric exposes capacity that is paid for but not used. It is tracked under operations, alongside stranded power and space per cabinet and floor loading limits, which means physical capacity and server use are measured together.

What the metric does not show is why servers are idle or what specific workloads are running. It only tells you the proportion of provisioned compute that is actually working over a period, not the cause of any gap.
